payload.scope: People made the thyroid cartilage construct to identify the paired laryngeal cartilage forming the anterior framework of the larynx and housing the vocal folds, so that clinicians can locate it for surgical landmarks, airway access, and voice disorder treatment.

definition.body: The thyroid cartilage is the human-authored anatomical construct identifying the paired laminae that fuse anteriorly to form the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple) and provide the anterior and lateral framework of the larynx, anchoring the vocal folds and intrinsic muscles. Parameters: (1) the laminae — two quadrilateral plates that meet at the anterior median angle; (2) the laryngeal prominence — the anterior ridge formed by the superior and inferior thyroid crests, palpable as the Adam's apple; (3) the superior and inferior horns — posterior extensions of each lamina providing attachment points for ligaments and membranes; (4) the external surface — attachments for the sternothyroid, thyrohyoid, and inferior constrictor muscles; (5) the internal surface — attachments for the thyrohyoid membrane and the vocal ligament. It persists as a standard anatomical landmark in human anatomy texts, laryngology, and airway management, providing the structural referent for laryngeal framework surgery, tracheostomy, and laryngoplasty procedures. e.g.: the thyroid cartilage anatomy shown in Gray's Anatomy, 51st edition; the laryngeal prominence palpated during thyroid examination per Bates' Guide to Physical Examination; open laryngectomy with thyroid cartilage resection for advanced glottic cancer per the VA Laryngeal Cancer Study | not: the cricoid cartilage (complete ring-shaped cartilage below the thyroid); the thyroid gland (endocrine organ, distinct from laryngeal cartilage) [formal: cartilago thyroidea | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]
